                                         Since its publication in 2020, the Neural Radiance Fields            bination of rendering mathematics and neural architectures
                                         (NeRF) paper [32] has spawned over 1,000 follow-ups. Yet,            leads to execution failures and large performance gaps. As
                                         unavailability of code or standardized implementations for           discussed in Section 2 and exhaustively shown in the Supple-
                                         most of them [50] means each subsequent work requires                mentary, recent advances like Paper2Code [42] and AutoP2C
                                         a significant effort to reimplement existing NeRF papers.            [25] – despite progress on general machine learning tasks –

reliably converts NeRF research papers into code that trains,         test-driven development with repository planning graphs

tations (Figure 1). Its success is based on five key technical        formulations. Paper2Agent [31] converts papers into con-
innovations. 1) Use of Nerfstudio [47] architecture as a              versational interfaces rather than trainable implementations.
context-free grammar (CFG) that encodes domain-aware                  Recent works [11, 65] explore fine-grained verification and
module compositions and interface contracts, leading to               dynamic planning, but remain domain-agnostic.

specialized agents that generate multi-file repositories in           systems proposing repository-level code generation [7, 16,
topological order, validating type signatures, tensor shapes          51, 52, 57, 61]. However, general software systems lack
and circular dependencies at each dependency before pro-              the mathematical understanding and architectural constraints
ceeding. 3) A compositional citation recovery that traverses          required for successful synthesis of research code.

Figure 2. N ERFIFY converts NeRF papers into code through four stages: (1) Agent parses and summarizes PDFs into simple markdown,
CFG from Nerfstudio and curated paper-code pairs as In-Context examples are saved in K (2) Compositional dependency resolution traverses
citation graphs to retrieve missing components from referenced papers, (3) GoT code synthesis generates repository files through specialized
agents operating in topological order (4) Visual refinement iteratively patches artifacts until achieving expert-level quality.

a state-of-the-art PDF-to-markdown conversion tool.
    As shown in Figure 2, the paper summarization agent
processes each document through multiple refinement stages.
First, MinerU converts the PDF into a structured markdown                  PlenOctrees    DyNeRF        Mip- NeRF    Instant- NGP
representation preserving equations, tables, figures, refer-
ences and implementation details. A subsequent cleaning
agent then distills this raw conversion by removing irrelevant
                                                                        TensoRF      NeRF-W        DONeRF           NeRV       EG3D
sections such as extended introductions, related work discus-
sions and redundant references. This agent operates under
strict preservation constraints: all equations, implementation                                          Mip- NeRF
pseudocode, architectural diagrams, and citation relation-                        Plenoxels
                                                                                                          360
ships must remain intact. The agent validates completeness
by ensuring that key technical components identified in the                                   K- Planes
abstract appear in the refined document. Each processed
paper and its corresponding Nerfstudio implementation are             Figure 3. NeRF citation dependency graphs. Implementing
then stored as structured examples in our knowledge base,             K-Planes requires retrieving components from 7 direct dependen-
forming the grammatical foundation that guides subsequent             cies (Plenoxels, TensoRF, Instant-NGP, Mip-NeRF 360, DyNeRF,
synthesis. Full details of the CFG formalization are provided         EG3D, NeRF-W) and 12 total papers with transitive dependencies.
in the supplementary material.                                        Our compositional citation recovery automatically traverses such
                                                                      graphs to identify and retrieve all necessary components.

Figure 4. Graph-of-Thought (GoT) Multi-Agent Code Synthesis. The master agent orchestrates specialized file-agents that progressively
build a NeRF repository over k steps. Each step shows files being created or modified through four stages: (1) DAG Construction maps
papers to Nerfstudio component dependencies, (2) Interface Freeze establishes API contracts in topological order, (3) Implementation
generates validated code with shape/gradient checks, (4) Integration Testing runs smoke tests with automated repair. Files evolve from
minimal interfaces to complete implementations as agents coordinate through the dependency graph, producing runnable NeRF plugins.


automated critique and repair loops when failures occur.                                                                                                                 critique agent produces no further feedback, (2) the maxi-
   The syntax and execution feedback loop iteratively re-                                                                                                                mum iteration count is reached, or (3) the implementation
fines code until all contracts pass, ensuring every generated                                                                                                            achieves the PSNR targets reported in the original paper.
repository can successfully train. This graph-native approach                                                                                                            This visual-driven approach consistently converges to within
enables component-level fault localization, yielding faster                                                                                                              0.5 dB PSNR and 0.2 SSIM of expert implementations.
convergence compared to monolithic code generation.

of floaters and ghosting. The semantics branch leverages                                                                                                                 isting benchmarks such as Paper2CodeBench, RexBench,

diagnoses with candidate patches.                                                                                                                                        generation, they lack the domain-specific evaluation criteria
